processing: Orthodox black tea, as its OP grade implies: withered, rolled, fully oxidised and fired.
harvest_season: Picked through the year; lots from the Uva quality season are the prized ones.
appearance_dry: Typical of orthodox Uva grades: dark, wiry leaf, sized by grade such as OP.
appearance_liquor: Typical of Uva: clear reddish amber.
appearance_wet: Coppery brown open leaf, as with other orthodox Ceylon teas.
taste_profile: No detailed tasting record was confirmed for this estate; expect the brisk, clean character typical of Uva rather than heavy malt.

brewing.notes: Western-style. Try the first cup plain before deciding on milk.

vintage_note: Sold by grade through the Colombo auction, in the Uva Medium category. As usual for Ceylon black tea, buy recent manufacture and drink within a year or two.
description:
Adawatte is an estate at Lunugala in Uva Province, making black tea. It is sold in the Uva Medium auction category, which is a useful thing to know before comparing it with the taller estates around Haputale.

Its record-setting lot was an OP, an orthodox leaf grade rather than CTC granules. What the garden tastes like in particular is little documented, so expect the general Uva character.

Brew it Western-style, with water just off the boil, for three to four minutes, and try it plain first.

When buying, ask for the grade and the manufacture date, and treat a seller who only says Ceylon or Uva with some caution.
history:
Its start date is not firmly established: one trade blog says 1938 and adds that the factory was rebuilt in 1956.

In 2022 it was reported as part of Hapugastenne Plantations, managed by Browns Plantations. That September an OP grade reached Rs. 2,250 per kg, an all-time record for the estate.
